component.name: g-helper-linux
component.summary: Performance, fan and battery control for ASUS laptops

description.p: g-helper-linux is a compact GTK4/libadwaita control centre for ASUS laptops, modelled on G-Helper for Windows. It talks to asusd for platform, fan, battery and keyboard control, and to cardwire for GPU blocking.

ul.li: Silent, Balanced and Turbo profiles with per-profile fan curves
PPT power limits and CPU energy preference
GPU modes through cardwire, plus firmware MUX and dGPU switches
Panel overdrive and refresh-rate switching
Battery charge limits and one-shot full charge
Keyboard lighting, Fn/ROG key mapping and a tray icon

description.p: Fan curves are edited as temperature/fan-speed charts, can be saved as named presets and shared as small JSON files. Hotkeys are read passively, so every key keeps its normal function, and the window opens next to the KDE panel wherever it is.
Reliable AC/battery profile switching and tuned-ppd coordination.

ul.li: Profile changes and AC/battery transitions now sync with tuned-ppd and power-profiles-daemon (org.freedesktop.UPower.PowerProfiles), preventing TuneD from reverting asusd back to Balanced on unplug.
Main window subscribes directly to asusd PlatformProfile and UPower OnBattery signals with transition guards so the window, overlay and tray stay in sync without flicker.
Tray dbusmenu layout revisions increment on profile and GPU updates, dbus-glib thread locks are initialized on startup, and --check now reports PowerProfiles status.

description.p: Multi-desktop display control, NVIDIA telemetry and lid lighting.

ul.li: Refresh-rate switching now supports GNOME (Mutter DisplayConfig D-Bus), Hyprland (hyprctl) and wlroots compositors (wlr-randr) alongside KDE Plasma.
Panel Overdrive is decoupled so it can still be toggled when refresh-rate control is unavailable.
Active proprietary NVIDIA dGPUs now report temperature and power through libnvidia-ml without waking runtime-suspended GPUs.
Added ROG Slash Lighting and AniMe Matrix controls in the main window and Settings, shown automatically on supported models.
Attach the GLib main loop before the first session-bus connection. The KWin placement helper now runs at startup, and an earlier connection left dbus-python unable to export the tray icon.
Starting hidden and closing to the tray work again, since both depended on that icon.
Regression tests cover the import order.
The mode card is centred on the whole screen and sits near the bottom edge, so a side panel no longer nudges it sideways.
The KWin placement watcher is loaded at startup, so the first card after a launch is positioned too.

description.p: Power-source memory and an on-screen mode card.

ul.li: Picking a mode remembers it for the current power source, so unplugging restores the battery mode and plugging back in restores the AC mode. asusd performs the switch itself, so it works while the window is closed.
A small dark card at the bottom of the screen names the mode after a plug or unplug, and after a hotkey or tray switch while the window is hidden.
Settings shows which mode is remembered for each power source.
The --profile command updates the same memory.

Headless smoke tests build the real application and open the main, Settings, Fans and Power, and Hotkeys windows, so a broken layout or a bad CSS selector fails the build instead of waiting for someone to click around.
GTK criticals are fatal in those tests, and they run in CI under Xvfb with private session and system buses.
Fans and Power names each auto-apply switch, keeps Apply Power Limits with the sliders, and uses the spare height for longer sliders.
Status text such as Applied and Listening on no longer looks like a clickable link.
Hotkeys opens compact, with a Mapped keys header, Clear all beside it and an empty-state hint.
The battery limit is labelled separately from live charge, and the keyboard colour swatch has a visible border and a tooltip.
Installs work from any prefix: the polkit policy follows the install prefix, the launcher records the rescan helper's directory, and the automation unit finds the binary through PATH.
--page opens only the requested window instead of showing the main window first, and the asusd banner shows the live error.
Settings no longer retries a failed refresh in a tight loop when asusd is unavailable.
AC/battery automation resumes after the user leaves Smart or Manual mode, and the tray keeps profile and GPU radios in separate groups.
CI checks the pip entry point and that the Makefile and install.sh stay in sync.
Refresh-rate control stays read-only with an explanation on desktops other than KDE Plasma, instead of failing with a KWin error.
The AppStream metadata links to the project homepage and issue tracker.
Packages are built for Debian and Ubuntu as well as Fedora.
The tray menu switches GPU modes (Eco, Standard, Smart, Optimized) as well as performance profiles.
Settings → Startup enables or disables the POST boot sound.
The GPU section and the tray tooltip say when a firmware change is waiting for a reboot.

description.p: Smart GPU mode and per-app dGPU access.

ul.li: Settings → dGPU Apps can keep the discrete GPU blocked, allowing only apps launched from that list to use it.
The GPU row names Smart and Manual modes instead of claiming Standard, with no preset highlighted for them.
AC/battery automation no longer overrides Smart or Manual.
GPU mode changes no longer stall the window or show raw cardwire errors when the dGPU is absent.
Silent, Balanced and Turbo profiles with editable fan curves and shareable presets.
GPU modes through cardwire, with Eco and Standard switching at runtime and no reboot.
Firmware MUX and dGPU switches, plus a Rescan dGPU action that brings the card back after ECO without rebooting.
Battery charge limit, one-shot full charge, and live charge, wattage and runtime readouts.
Keyboard Aura lighting and Fn/ROG key mapping through a passive evdev reader.
Refresh-rate switching and per-app dGPU launching.
The window opens next to the KDE panel on any screen edge.
